objects.original: Two completed Ito rows X,Y and a fixed coarse dyadic cutoff tau.
objects.reconstructed: Write R_+=[0,infinity), and let lambda_T be Lebesgue measure on [0,T], transported to R_+ (the given comap of volume restricted to [0,T]). All time integrals below use this measure unless indicated otherwise. For n in N put t[n,i]=i*T/2^n for i=0,...,2^n, and Delta_i^n Z=Z(t[n,i+1])-Z(t[n,i]). A ProgressiveL2Integrand eta on horizon T is a real process eta(t,omega), strongly progressive for the filtration, with (omega,t) -> eta(t,omega) in L^2(mu x lambda_T). I_T^j(eta) denotes the supplied completed continuous Ito process driven by the scalar coordinate B_j(t,omega)=(B(t,omega))_j: the pointwise limit of chosen elementary stochastic-integral approximations off their null uniform-Cauchy bad set, zero on that bad set, and held constant after T; at each t<=T it agrees almost everywhere with the L^2-completion integral up to t. Set X=A+sum_j I_T^j(eta_j), Y=C+sum_j I_T^j(xi_j), and tau=t[m,k]. The integrand's toLp operation is its L^2 equivalence class represented by (omega,t)->eta(t,omega).
objects.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoDyadicPrefixCrossQV.lean:28; X,Y,Z and I plus all use the same coordinateFamily hB.

domains.original: Finite measure and coordinate type, usual filtration, T>0; tau=kT/2^m.
domains.reconstructed: Omega measurable; J finite with decidable equality; mu finite; R_+-filtration; T>0; B:R_+ x Omega->R^J standard vector Brownian; eta,xi:J->ProgressiveL2Integrand(filtration,mu,T); A,C:R_+ x Omega->R; m in N; k in {0,...,2^m}.
domains.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoDyadicPrefixCrossQV.lean:28; m,k parameterize a coarse endpoint and Iic tau restricts the horizon measure.

quantifiers.original: For every fixed m,k, let fine level n→infinity.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Universally all data in displayed order: spaces,filtration,mu,T,B; Brownian,positive-horizon,usual hypotheses; eta,xi; A,C; slice measurability for A,C; their path assumptions; m,k. Then n tends to infinity.
quantifiers.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoDyadicPrefixCrossQV.lean:28; The m,k binders precede TendstoInMeasure; no random cutoff is introduced.

assumptions.original: Same vector Brownian driver; progressive L² rows; a.e. measurable drift slices and continuous BV drift paths.
assumptions.reconstructed: The vector Brownian hypothesis means B(0,omega)=0 for every omega; increments on finite families of pairwise disjoint half-open intervals are jointly independent; every continuous real linear functional ell sends B(t)-B(s), s<t, to a centered Gaussian of variance (t-s)||ell||^2; paths are mu-almost surely continuous. B is strongly adapted, and for every s<=t the increment B(t)-B(s) is independent of the sigma-algebra filtration(s). The filtration is right continuous, and every mu-null subset of Omega belongs to filtration(t) for every t>=0 (completeness at each time). For each t<=T, A_t and C_t are mu-a.e. strongly measurable. For mu-a.e. omega, A(.,omega) is continuous and of bounded variation on [0,T]; the same separate a.e. assertion holds for C. No adaptedness of A or C is assumed.
assumptions.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoDyadicPrefixCrossQV.lean:28; The private BV-add helper derives the sum drift property internally; it is not a new hypothesis.

conclusion.original: Inclusive fine-cell product sum converges in measure to sum of integrals eta_j xi_j over [0,tau].
conclusion.reconstructed: As n->infinity, sum_{i=0}^{2^n-1} 1_{t[n,i+1]<=tau}*Delta_i^n X*Delta_i^n Y converges in mu-measure to sum_j integral_{s<=tau} eta_j(s,omega)*xi_j(s,omega) d lambda_T(s).
conclusion.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoDyadicPrefixCrossQV.lean:28; hPolar proves discrete polarization; hEnergy proves integral polarization before taking the limit.

scopes.original: A fixed cutoff including 0,T; no uniform-in-cutoff convergence.
scopes.reconstructed: The target time tau is any fixed point of any fixed dyadic level m. This is convergence in measure of real random variables: for each epsilon>0, mu{|difference|>=epsilon}->0 (equivalently with >). It is neither a stated pathwise convergence nor a uniform-in-tau claim. Restrictions s<=tau and right endpoints<=tau are inclusive.
scopes.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoDyadicPrefixCrossQV.lean:28; hGrid intersects finite coordinate/time equality events; ae_all_iff collects levels for the subsequence argument.

constant_dependencies.original: No deterministic variation or rate constant.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: No bound constant is quantified. The convergence may depend on T,B,filtration,mu,eta,xi,A,C,m,k. The finite variation bound may depend on omega and is not uniformly bounded by a given constant.
constant_dependencies.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoDyadicPrefixCrossQV.lean:28; The proof adds no uniform BV bound.
